Thanks for the signal and logs, Tessa / Anika. Initial read: the traces show the request failing during the prefetch handshake (timeout in our kv-cache connect path) on a subset of requests with ~2% frequency for this tenant. I don't see an obvious model-level regression in the kernel logs; this looks infra-level (handshake/connection negotiation) and correlates with a burst of parallel prefetch attempts from the customer's demo harness.

Immediate mitigations we can try (fastest first):
1) Disable prefetch for CobaltAI tenant via routing override — this will route their requests to the non-prefetch path; expected impact: higher token cost, lower tail latency variance.
2) Reduce the prefetch concurrency cap for the tenant (soft throttle) — keeps prefetch on but limits burst behavior.
3) Apply a temporary per-tenant handshake timeout bump while we collect richer traces.

I'll spin up a quick test in staging (replay their logs) and report back within 2h. If we can't get the mitigation in production in that window, we should allow a short SLO exception for the demo window — please confirm owner for approval.

Questions for Sales/CS:
- Is CobaltAI ok with disabling prefetch for the demo (they'll accept a minor cost increase)?
- Do we want to make this an account-scoped flag in the console so we don't need prod-side patching?

—Dev

A) Runtime toggle (fastest): add an account-scoped boolean in our routing layer to bypass prefetch for account COB-47. I can push the routing override now; no infra deploy needed.

B) Product follow-up (next week): expose a per-account prefetch cap + an "experiment" flag in Console so Sales can flip for demos. That work is a small Console + policy change; estimate 1 sprint.

Given the demo timeline, I recommend option A now, and we create a Console ticket for B (assign to product).

I'll apply the routing override at 09:30 PST and confirm. If we need the SLO exemption paperwork, Marissa — can you confirm and send the short note? We'll mark this as a customer-impact operational tweak (no config change persisted beyond request).
